demo_orders.context:
All monetary amounts are integer cents; do not convert units. Order statuses: completed/pending/cancelled. Cities: Beijing/Shanghai/Shenzhen.
Order analytics interpretation and SQL checks:
- Respect the question's explicit scope. Counts and lists use all order statuses unless a status is explicitly requested. Only revenue defaults to completed. "All statuses" means no status predicate; it does not request grouping by status.
- A total count asks for one count column. Group by status/month/city only when the question requests that breakdown.
- Average completed-order amount requires filtering to completed orders BEFORE the per-order sum, then averaging those sums. Do not average all statuses or individual line items.
- SELECT exactly the requested outputs in the requested order. An ID used only to order/group rows must stay outside SELECT. Group customers by their ID when names can repeat.
- Use only tables needed for the requested outputs or conditions. Qualify ambiguous column names when joining. Prefer a direct aggregate with ORDER BY and LIMIT for a top result over unnecessary nested MAX subqueries.
- For entities with no related record, preserve the entity table with NOT EXISTS or LEFT JOIN and a NULL check on the related key; do not reverse the outer join.
- Use SQLite syntax. Removing every occurrence of a substring uses replace(text, old, new). TRIM(BOTH ... FROM ...) is not SQLite syntax.

business_orders_v1.context:
This is synthetic acceptance data, not production orders. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD in 2026. All monetary values are integer cents; preserve cents in answers. Revenue includes only completed orders and is SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price_cents), using historical item prices, not products.price_cents. Include pending/cancelled only when asked. City/category/name/sku values are case-sensitive text. Names may repeat; customer_id identifies people.
